subject: Request: temporary SLA carve-out for moderation webhook timeouts + structured-output rollback path
messages:
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@meridian-pay.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: security@meridian-pay.com
Date: 2027-05-09T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent moderation webhook timeouts affecting tokenized receipts workflow

Hi Vanessa,

Hope you're well. Over the last 48 hours we've observed a spike in moderation-related timeouts from Redwood's moderation webhook when our payout-receipt extraction job calls the tool-calling filter. The symptom: ~1.8% of calls return 504/timeout (sample attached) which causes our downstream structured-output validator to drop payloads and fail the transaction flow.

This is showing up as a material operational impact (customers see payment delays and we cannot reconcile receipts). Given our contract's 99.9% uptime target for the inference route, we need to understand whether Redwood can:

- confirm root cause (runtime vs toolchain routing),
- propose a short-term mitigation (graceful fallback or cached allow-list), and
- agree to a temporary carve-out (or alternative SLA) for calls routed to the third-party filter while you deploy the mitigation.

I've attached a log excerpt and a small sample of failed structured-output payloads. We're requesting a formal carve-out window (up to 30 days) while Meridian accepts a fallback mode that uses an internal light-touch filter we manage, provided Redwood supplies a signed exception and a remediation timeline.

Can we schedule a call today for triage? We'd like names for the engineers and an expected ETA for a rollback/mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Anna Liu
Senior Product Ops
Meridian Payments

Attachments: moderation-timeout-sample.log, structured-output-failures-samples.json

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@meridian-pay.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent moderation webhook timeouts affecting tokenized receipts workflow

Anna,

Thanks for the heads-up and the samples — that's helpful. Sorry for the disruption. I'm looping in Karthik (product) and Marissa (legal) so we can triage and get an exception process started. Quick answers up-front:

- We'd like to confirm whether the 504s are originating from our moderation filter service or from the tool-calling proxy layer. Initial logs suggest a transient connection saturation on the filter side, but we need a deeper look.
- Short-term mitigation ideas: (1) automatic client-side retry with exponential backoff (we can share a recommended library and config), (2) a limited fallback that routes to Redwood's internal low-latency heuristic filter (no external webhook) for your high-priority route, or (3) per-route prefix caching for known-safe tokens.
- About the carve-out: we can put a temporary SLA amendment that explicitly enumerates calls routed to external moderation webhooks and defines an alternate SLO (e.g., 95% success for those calls) during the mitigation window. We'll need Meridian signoff and a remediation timeline.

Proposed next steps:
1) Triage call today at 11:30 PT — Karthik will drive technical triage.
2) Redwood to provide a drafted carve-out addendum + rollback plan within 48 hours (Marissa will prepare).
3) Exchange a short-term runbook and retry settings to test immediately.

If that works, I'd like the call invite and a short list of impacted request IDs so we can correlate.

-Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

> On May 9, 2027, at 08:12, Anna Liu <anna.liu@meridian-pay.com> wrote:
> ... (attached logs)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Anna Liu <anna.liu@meridian-pay.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent moderation webhook timeouts affecting tokenized receipts workflow

Anna, Vanessa,

Thanks for bringing this up. Quick technical summary from our side after a first-pass investigation:

- Root cause hypothesis: connection queueing in the external moderation filter (your webhook endpoint) combined with the tool-calling proxy's default 3s per-call timeout can lead to flaky timeouts when the filter briefly hits a multi-second tail. The structured-output validator then rejects incomplete JSON payloads, causing the flow to abort.
- Evidence: attached samples show the proxy returning an upstream 504 after 3s and the subsequent validator error. We also saw a small increase in latencies on the proxy during the incident window.

Temporary mitigations we can push today (non-invasive):
- Increase upstream timeout to 8s for the specific route while we monitor (config change, low risk).
- Automatic soft-fallback: if moderation webhook does not respond in 8s, route to Redwood's internal minimal filter for classification only (low-latency heuristic) and tag the payload with "filter_fallback":true so Meridian can audit results.
- Send you a suggested client-side retry policy (2 retries, jittered) and a small cache for recently-allowed token prefixes to reduce calls.

Proposed SLA carve-out language (draft bullets):
- Effective window: 2027-05-10 to 2027-06-09 (30 days)
- Scope: calls to endpoint /v1/tools/moderation-webhook that are routed to a third-party webhook configured in Meridian's account.
- Temporary SLO: 95% successful tool-calls (response within 8s) during the window; all other Redwood SLOs remain unchanged.
- Operational commitments: Redwood will (a) provide 24/7 on-call for triage during first 72 hours, (b) publish post-incident analysis weekly, and (c) implement a permanent fix or capacity increase by 2027-06-05.
- Auditability: Redwood will attach filter_fallback flags and produce a daily CSV of fallback events.

If Meridian accepts this language we will convert it to a formal addendum and send for signature. Also cc Legal for the wording and any credit/repudiation language.

Karthik
Director, Product, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@meridian-pay.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-12T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent moderation webhook timeouts affecting tokenized receipts workflow — carve-out agreed pending signature

Anna,

Appreciate the sync earlier today. Summary and next steps below.

Agreed interim plan (formal addendum attached):
- Carve-out window: 2027-05-10 to 2027-06-09 (30 days).
- Scope: calls routed to Meridian-configured third-party moderation webhooks only.
- Interim SLO for those calls: 95% success within 8s. Redwood will mark any fallback events with filter_fallback=true and deliver daily CSVs.
- Temporary operational commitments: Redwood will keep an on-call engineer assigned for 72 hours and deliver weekly post-incident notes.
- Permanent remediation target: capacity/config rollout by 2027-06-05; if not met, we'll propose a compensating credit aligned to the contract's credit matrix (Marissa will insert exact credit language).

Attached: proposed-carveout-and-rollback-plan.md (wording for addendum), moderation-timeout-sample.log, structured-output-failures-samples.json.

Action items:
1) Marissa: finalize addendum text and include contract credit clause (ETA 48 hours).
2) Meridian: please confirm list of endpoints to which this carve-out should apply (we currently have /v1/tools/moderation-webhook on your account).
3) Karthik/Infra: flip the 8s route timeout and enable fallback flagging tonight in the canary region; we will monitor and share daily metrics.
4) Anna: sign the DocuSign when received.

If Meridian confirms endpoints by EOD we will generate the DocuSign and route to your Legal.

Thanks — we'd like to keep this narrow to avoid broadening the exception baseline.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
